_comment: AI-Assisted: Claude Code (model: claude-opus-5) - Authored the published-bundle schema per curated-snapshot-format.md §3-§4 (task T033) against reference-db-schema.md v1.2.0. One array per consumer table, named in lowerCamelCase, each element carrying exactly that table's columns in lowerCamelCase, so the ingestor is a mechanical array-to-table load with no reshaping. Arrays are sorted by their table's primary key, which is what makes the bundle byte-stable and a hand-diff of two bundles meaningful during an incident. Absent optionals are OMITTED (§5) and ingested as SQL NULL; no property here is nullable. datasheetDetachmentEligibility is ALWAYS PRESENT and ALWAYS EMPTY: no upstream datasheet-to-detachment join exists, so the consumer contract's default (absence = legal in any detachment of its faction) applies, which is the correct non-fabricating behaviour under FR-019. additionalProperties is false throughout so an unmapped field is a build failure rather than a silent omission. 004-rules-data-enrichment adds datasheetCompositions, datasheetOptionGroups and datasheetOptionChoices, plus chapterKeywords (T040), factionRules (T048), detachmentRules (T055) and keywordGlossary (T062), and the optional wargearOptionState, keywordClass and armyRuleState columns, per contracts/bundle-schema-delta.md. Every one of those is ADDITIVE: bundleFormatVersion stays 1 because the layout rules are unchanged, and an existing row that acquires no new value is byte-identical to what it was.
title: Published snapshot bundle rules-<rulesVersionId>.json

bundleFormatVersion.description: This document's MAJOR. Distinct from snapshotMeta.schemaContractVersion, which is the CONSUMER contract's MAJOR: the first describes how the document is laid out, the second describes what the app must be able to read.

publishedAt.description: ISO-8601 UTC. The ONLY timestamp anywhere in the bundle, and an explicit build input rather than 'now' -- that is what makes a rebuild byte-identical (FR-033, SC-006).

sourceNote.description: Authored, factual provenance. Carries no endorsement claim (FR-050).

valueJson.description: The rule value serialised with the canonical serialiser, so the emission is byte-stable.

gameSizeRules.description: Sorted by id. Bands must be contiguous, non-overlapping, and cover reference-db-schema.md §3.4's declared range end to end.

armyRuleState.description: 004 additive column. 'none' = this faction genuinely has no army rule, a completed curation decision that contributes nothing to the coverage denominator. OMITTED = not yet curated, which is a DIFFERENT fact (004 FR-021); a consumer that cannot tell the two apart shows the same empty section for both.

factionRules.description: Sorted by id. One row per army rule, from 004-rules-data-enrichment; a faction may have more than one, which is what displayOrder is for. The NAME is always carried. The `summary` is authored by a human from the mechanic and appears only once approved: an unapproved entry ships with its name alone, because publishing a draft would put wording nobody has signed off in front of every player (004 FR-021, FR-024, contracts/authored-summary-gates.md §3).

detachmentRules.description: Sorted by id. One row per detachment rule, from 004-rules-data-enrichment; a detachment may own more than one, which is why the RULE rather than the detachment is the key. The NAME comes from the source and is ALWAYS carried (004 FR-022) -- a detachment whose authoring campaign has not started still ships every rule it owns, named and unexplained, and is counted in the coverage report. The `summary` is authored by a human from the mechanic and appears only once approved. Two detachments in different factions sharing a rule name emit two rows with DIFFERENT ids, because the id embeds the detachment id.

keywordGlossary.description: Sorted by keywordKey. Authored keyword definitions, from 004-rules-data-enrichment. keywordKey is the NORMATIVE normalised key of contracts/bundle-schema-delta.md §4 -- NFKC, casefold, non-alphanumerics to spaces, collapse whitespace, then strip a trailing integer parameter -- which both producer and consumer MUST derive by that exact procedure or a lookup silently fails to resolve. One entry therefore serves a keyword and every casing, spacing, punctuation and numeric-parameter variant of it. An entry exists ONLY when authored and approved; an unauthored keyword has no row here, still appears on its datasheets and weapons unchanged, and is named in the coverage report (004 FR-023).

detachmentRestrictions.description: Sorted by id. detachmentId omitted = an edition-wide rule.

enhancementEligibility.description: Sorted by (enhancementId, ruleType, value). No rows for an enhancement = offered to any Character.

detailEditionCode.description: Omitted when the detail came from the snapshot's own edition (§5). Present, this makes a hybrid entity self-describing (C5/R4).

wargearOptionState.description: 004 additive column. Distinguishes a datasheet with genuinely no options from one whose options failed to extract (004 FR-016). OMITTED = the detail source was not consulted, which is a third fact again, and an existing row that acquires no value stays byte-identical to what it is today.

keywordClass.description: 004 additive column. OMITTED = unclassified, which is not a defect and blocks nothing: an unclassified keyword's row is byte-identical to what it is today and KWD-UNCLASSIFIED (advisory) names it in the report (004 FR-020).

chapterKeywords.description: Sorted by keyword. The enumerable chapter (sub-faction) vocabulary, from 004-rules-data-enrichment. Keyed by keyword ALONE because 004 FR-019 guarantees one parent per chapter keyword, which is what keeps 'resolve a chapter -> its datasheets' a plain join against datasheetKeywords.keyword. A chapter the points source already models as a faction of its own STILL appears here, flagged (004 FR-018), so consumers have one mechanism for every chapter grouping.

chapterFactionId.description: Present when the points source models this chapter as a faction of its own. That faction's own parentFactionId MUST equal this row's; a contradiction is the blocking KWD-CHAPTER-PARENT-CONFLICT.

abilityKeywords.description: Comma-separated keywords only -- 'lethal hits,rapid fire 1'. Never rules text.

datasheetAbilities.description: Sorted by (datasheetId, name). Expanded from the curated ability_keys against curation/abilities/**; every summary is non-empty and approved (V7).

summary.description: An ORIGINAL, MECHANICS-ONLY summary authored for this data set, target <= 1000 characters. Never the publisher's rules text and never a light rewording of it (reference-db-schema.md §6.1).

datasheetCosts.description: Sorted by (datasheetId, modelCount). Exactly the copy_index_min = 1 projection of datasheetCostTiers -- the redundancy is deliberate and is what lets a v1.1.0 app read this table unchanged (guarantee 7).

datasheetCostTiers.description: Sorted by (datasheetId, modelCount, copyIndexMin). The full copy-indexed set.

datasheetCostContexts.description: Sorted by (datasheetId, pricingContext, modelCount, copyIndexMin). The prices the points source states a CONDITION for: a unit its own faction prices one way and another army prices another ('every-model-has-imperium'), or two bands of one unit that hold the same number of models and are told apart only by what they contain ('with-hunting-wolves'). Deliberately a separate array: datasheetCosts and datasheetCostTiers carry the unconditional price and only that, so their primary keys are unchanged and a consumer that does not read this array reads exactly the prices it read before. Absence of a row here is not a missing price -- it means the unit is priced one way whatever the condition.

datasheetWargearOptions.description: Sorted by id. Cost-bearing options only.

datasheetCompositions.description: Sorted by (datasheetId, line). One entry per model line, from 004-rules-data-enrichment. A datasheet whose composition could not be resolved carries NO ROWS AT ALL rather than partial ones (004 FR-008): a partial composition is worse than none, and a guessed count mis-prices a unit. minCount == maxCount is a FIXED count -- the majority shape -- and is never missing data.

modelLine.description: FK to datasheetModels.line. OMITTED when the name match was not unique -- never guessed.

datasheetOptionGroups.description: Sorted by id. One group per source option row. id derives from the source's own line ordinal, which is what makes an upstream relabelling surface as a RENAME rather than a removal plus an addition (004 FR-015). scopeN is present exactly when scope is per_n_models.

datasheetOptionChoices.description: Sorted by id. A choice is a NAME plus mechanical values -- there is deliberately no description property, which is what stops this class becoming a prose channel (004 FR-016). pointsDelta is OMITTED, never 0, when the points source does not price the choice (004 FR-013, guarantee 10): a consumer reads 'uncosted', never 'free'. isNoChange marks an explicit 'no change' alternative, which is never published with a price at all.

grantsWeaponLine.description: FK to datasheetWeapons.line. OMITTED when the name match is not unique -- never guessed and never silently attached to the wrong profile (004 FR-011).

pricedOptionId.description: FK to datasheetWargearOptions.id. OMITTED when the points source does not price this choice.

datasheetDetachmentEligibility.description: ALWAYS EMPTY. No upstream datasheet-to-detachment join exists, so the consumer contract's default applies: absence of rows = legal in any detachment of its faction.
